title: Console frontend: Dedicated staged rollout pages + stage detail (gates, approvals, error states)
creator: Dylan Brooks
project: Dedicated staged rollouts for reserved pools
description:
Build the Console UI for Dedicated staged rollouts: list + detail pages, stage detail view, gate status badges, approvals/abort modal flows, and robust error/empty states. This is the customer/operator-facing surface for the new control plane objects (RolloutPlan/Stage/Gate) and is required for dogfood + beta pilots.

Primary users (v1): Redwood operators + enterprise opt-in Dedicated admins. UI must respect RBAC and fail safe (no accidental progression).

Scope (frontend):
- Dedicated Pool > Rollouts tab: staged rollouts list (active + recent) with status, current stage, last updated, and quick actions.
- Rollout detail page: stage timeline, current stage banner, traffic weight display per stage, and gate evaluation summary.
- Stage detail view: full gate list w/ per-gate status + reason, evaluation window details, and links to relevant dashboards.
- Approvals modal: manual approval (advance stage), abort rollout, rollback-to-previous (if supported by backend), with confirmation, audit note field, and permission checks.
- Gate badges: consistent iconography + tooltip text across list/detail components.
- Error states: missing metrics -> show “Hold (metrics unavailable)” with guidance; evaluator degraded -> show “Hold (system)” and prevent actions; API errors -> retry UI + error copy.

Out of scope:
- Editing rollout plans (creation wizard) beyond link-out to internal admin flows if needed; we’ll prioritize view/operate for beta.
- Full A/B experiment UI (separate workstream).

Design references:
- DES-133 (Console staged rollout workflow for Dedicated pools)
- Wireframes: Drive doc console-rollouts-ui-wireframes-dedicated.json

Backend/API dependencies:
- ENG-5126 status aggregation endpoint + websocket/polling contract
- ENG-5122 approvals/abort endpoints
- ENG-5129 RBAC permissions (rollout.approve / rollout.abort / rollout.edit)

Success criteria:
- Operators can reliably see which stage is live, why we’re held, and what action is needed.
- UI is resilient to partial/late data (no infinite spinners; always shows last-known + timestamp + refresh).
- Correct gating visualization prevents accidental advancement when gates are failing or data is missing.
acceptance_criteria: Dedicated pool page shows a Rollouts tab with staged rollouts list (supports empty state, loading, and error state).
Rollout detail route renders stage timeline with current stage highlighted and traffic weights per stage displayed.
Stage detail view shows all gates with status (PASS/FAIL/HOLD/UNKNOWN), threshold summary, evaluation window, and last evaluated timestamp.
Approvals modal supports: advance stage (manual approve), abort rollout; each action requires confirmation and displays permission-based disable states.
RBAC is enforced in UI: missing permissions hides or disables actions and shows explanatory copy (no client-side only gating; must align with 403 handling).
All API failures have deterministic UX: toast + inline error, retry affordance, and no stuck loading states.
Gate status badges are reusable components with tooltips and consistent mapping to backend enums.
Audit note field is present in approve/abort modal and is passed through to backend when supported; otherwise gated off with feature flag and copy.
Basic accessibility: keyboard navigation for modal, aria labels for badges/tooltips, and empty/error states meet Redwood Console standards.
implementation_notes:
Frontend stack assumptions: Redwood Console (React + TypeScript) using existing router + query client patterns. Prefer polling for v1; add websocket subscription when ENG-5126 exposes stable stream.

Data contracts (assumptions; verify against ENG-5126/ENG-5122):
- Rollout summary includes: rollout_id, pool_id, tenant_id, status, current_stage_id, created_at, updated_at.
- Stage includes: stage_id, name, traffic_weight, requires_approval, state, started_at, completed_at.
- Gate summary includes: gate_id, type, status, last_evaluated_at, window, threshold, observed_value, reason.

UI state mapping guidance:
- If any gate status = FAIL => stage banner shows "Held (gate failed)" and actions limited to Abort (and Rollback if supported).
- If any gate status = HOLD/UNKNOWN due to missing metrics => stage banner "Held (metrics unavailable)"; disable Approve; show troubleshooting link.
- If evaluator health indicates degraded => stage banner "Held (system)"; disable Approve; show incident/runbook link.

Feature flags:
- dedicatedStagedRolloutsEnabled (global)
- dedicatedStagedRolloutsTenantAllowlist (only show tab when enabled for tenant unless operator override)

Telemetry (frontend):
- Track page views + action clicks: rollout_detail_view, stage_detail_view, approve_click, abort_click, retry_click.
- Track error toasts grouped by error_code to avoid high cardinality.

risks: Backend contract churn (state naming + enums) could cause rework; mitigate by isolating mapping in a single adapter module.
Metrics missing/late is common; UI must avoid ambiguous "Unknown" without guidance; include explicit freshness and 'why held' text.
RBAC/tenant allowlist complexity: ensure tab visibility and action buttons are consistent with server-side checks; test 403/404 paths.
test_plan:
Unit tests: enum->badge mapping; permission gating; error boundary rendering.

Integration (staging):
1) Load dedicated pool with active rollout; verify list + detail + stage detail renders.
2) Simulate failing gate -> UI shows Held (gate failed), Approve disabled, Abort enabled.
3) Simulate missing metrics -> UI shows Held (metrics unavailable) with last-evaluated timestamp and refresh.
4) Simulate 403 for approve -> action disabled + server error handling if forced; no progression.
5) Simulate backend timeout -> retry UI appears; page does not spin indefinitely.

E2E: covered in ENG-5132 once routes are stable.
open_questions: Do we expose a "Rollback" action in v1 UI, or only Abort? Depends on backend semantics and safety guardrails.
What is the canonical difference between rollout.state=PAUSED vs stage.state=HELD vs stage.state=WAITING_APPROVAL? Need final state machine from ENG-5126.
Do we show traffic weights as requested config or effective weight after routing guardrails (e.g., min headroom adjustments)? If both exist, label clearly.
